First, the vertical-space problem: page 6 uses roughly the top fifth of the page for the three big stat figures (12/34, 21/34, 4) and leaves the bottom four-fifths blank; page 8's entire Exemption Process is nine short numbered lines with the rest of the page empty; page 10's Appendix A checklist ends a third of the way down. Three near-empty pages in a ten-page standard means the section-per-page rule is being applied mechanically rather than to serve the reader. Second, the gap assessment on page 6 is the one place the brief asked for analysis and it is three unlabelled numerals with tiny captions — no per-service breakdown, no named boundaries (the brief says trace context is dropped at four service boundaries and page 6 says only "service boundaries currently drop trace context" without naming them), and no unit or denominator on the standalone "4". The rollout table on page 7 does the opposite well: dated milestones with explicit requirements. Genericness: the content is unmistakably this brief — 34 services, the 12/21/4 baseline, the three-quarter rollout, W3C trace context, the [service].request.count metric pattern — but the visual shell is the default single-column Word standard with a red accent rule; swap the words and the same shell serves any policy document. Not shippable unchanged: pages 6, 8 and 10 need to be consolidated or filled, and the gap assessment needs the four boundaries named.

Integrity fails on page 1: the "Contents" heading is followed by roughly a third of a page of white space with no table of contents entries — the TOC field rendered empty, leaving a labelled but unfilled block above the Executive Summary rule. That alone caps the document at level 1, and no amount of downstream polish compensates. Elsewhere the work is actually competent: the KPI band on page 1 (1.4B rows / 6,000 writes per sec / 31 hours / 4 deploys) is well set with units and captions, the Current/Target Schema tables on page 2 carry a Notes column that does real work ("Dropped in Phase 4 (Contract)"), and the four phase pages repeat Actions / Exit Criteria / Rollback in the same order with the same rule-under-heading treatment. Two secondary problems: the schema table continuation at the top of page 3 and the monitoring table continuation at the top of page 7 both start a page as a bare header-plus-three-rows fragment with no lead-in, so the reader meets a table before its title; and the Failure Modes table on page 7 sets five columns of small text at a size that is noticeably tighter than every other table in the document, breaking the type rhythm. Content-wise it answers the brief closely — dual-write window, pausable backfill, per-phase rollback with data-loss risk and time-to-rollback in the appendix. Visually it is a conventional red-rule-on-white report; the KPI strip is the only element that would not appear unchanged in any other engineering plan.

Integrity holds: no clipped or empty frames, no placeholder text; the running header ("Authentication Service — Security Review · Confidential") and footer ("Confidential — Internal Distribution Only") repeat on pages 2–11, and the p5→p6 spill of finding H-2 continues cleanly mid-sentence at the 'POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm' step. Legibility is fine for an on-screen/print report: single measure, generous margins, dark text on white. Coherence holds — the three 'Detailed Findings — {High,Medium,Low} Severity' section openers on p5, p7 and p9 use identical treatment, and every finding block on p5–p10 repeats the same Severity/Status/Affected-component line followed by bold-lead paragraphs (Reproduction, Impact, Remediation, Remediation effort). Communicative effectiveness is largely met: the p2 stat row (9 / 2 / 4 / 3 with Total, High, Medium, Low labels) plus the '9 eng-days' callout carries the brief's headline numbers with units; the p4 findings table gives ID, Finding, Severity, Status for all nine and its caption states what severity and status mean; every finding title asserts a conclusion (e.g. 'M-2 — Persistent "remember me" cookie has no idle timeout'), and p11 closes with an explicit 'Overall assessment ... Low-to-Medium' verdict. Craft falls short of level 5. Severity is never visually encoded — 'High' and 'Low' are the same small grey text in the p4 table and in the finding metadata lines, so a nine-finding report cannot be scanned by risk. The detailed findings (p7, p8, p9, p10) are undifferentiated grey paragraph runs with no rule, tint or indent separating Reproduction from Remediation. Page 6 carries only a third of a page of H-2 continuation and then two-thirds white before the medium section starts on p7, and the p11 Residual Risk page is five unstructured paragraphs where a residual-severity table or before/after comparison was the obvious move given the '9 eng-days' framing. The p1 cover is a centred title plus a flat one-level contents list with no page numbers.

On genericness: apart from the p2 numeric stat strip, nothing here is specific to a security assessment. It is entirely black-and-white with a single dark table header row on p4; swap the headings and the same shell would serve an audit, a due-diligence memo or a process review without a pixel changing.
